niche: Mind Hacks, AI Secrets, Bizarre Body Science & Hidden Power Dynamics

ideas.title: The Hidden Setting Draining Your Battery and Privacy
ideas.angle: The video reveals a specific deep-layer smartphone setting—Significant Locations or System Services—that maps every movement. It challenges the viewer to check it right now to see their own 'secret map,' triggering comments from shocked users.

hook.en: Turn off this one setting immediately.

ideas.reason: Privacy-centric 'check your phone' videos consistently hit 80%+ VVSA because they offer immediate utility and a sense of 'hidden danger' that compels users to share and comment their findings.
sources: Google Account Help: Manage your Location History
Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) Mobile Device Best Practices

ideas.title: How AI Knows You're Lying via Your Eyes
ideas.angle: Shows how modern AI algorithms track micro-dilations in pupils to detect stress or deceit. It includes a 5-second 'stare challenge' where the viewer has to keep their eyes still, driving up retention and comments about failing the test.

hook.en: Your eyes are leaking your secrets.

ideas.reason: Eye-tracking and 'glitch' content is currently surging on TikTok/Shorts. Combining it with 'AI detection' taps into the 'Hidden Tech Secrets' pillar and provides a high-retention interactive challenge.
sources: Nature: Automated pupil tracking for psychological research
MIT Technology Review: AI-based lie detection and biometric monitoring
Journal of Vision: Pupil diameter as a measure of cognitive load

ideas.title: The Screen Glitch You Can't Unsee
ideas.angle: A visual 'system exploit' for the human brain. It uses a specific high-contrast optical illusion to create a 'dead pixel' effect in the viewer's vision for 10 seconds. It forces the user to rewatch to confirm the effect, driving APV over 100%.

hook.en: Stare at the center right now.

ideas.reason: Interactive 'visual hacks' have the highest VVSA in the 'Bizarre Body/Brain Glitches' category. They function as a 'live test' that requires the viewer to stay until the very end to see the result.
sources: Scientific American: How Optical Illusions Trick Your Brain
Journal of Neuroscience: Neural mechanisms of visual disappearance
